questions.question: What is a processed material? Name four processed materials used in a building and one property of each.
questions.expected_answer: A processed material is made by changing raw materials. Examples: concrete, strong and hard; plaster of Paris, sets quickly into any shape; ceramic tiles, hard and easy to clean; glass, see-through and hard; plastic pipes, light and waterproof; paint, colourful and protective; fabric curtains, soft and colourful.

questions.question: How are glass and plastics made, and why is plastic waste a problem?
questions.expected_answer: Glass is made by melting sand, soda ash and limestone at a very high temperature and letting it cool. Most plastics are made from crude oil, and some in South Africa from coal. Plastic waste is a problem because plastic does not rot, so it stays in the environment for hundreds of years, polluting rivers and harming animals.

questions.question: Name two natural fibres and one synthetic fibre, and say where each comes from. What does paint do?
questions.expected_answer: Natural fibres: cotton from the cotton plant, wool from sheep, mohair from Angora goats. Synthetic fibres: nylon or polyester, made from oil. Paint colours surfaces and protects them, stopping steel from rusting, wood from rotting and rain from getting into walls.
